requirement.title: Enable and disable managed accounts
requirement.summary: Add a persisted account availability state with immediate old-session revocation and a working admin filter/edit flow.

sources.content: Add enabled/disabled account state with filtering, editing and disabled-user access revocation; use a small existing web admin project for SDLC validation.

goals.problem: An account cannot currently be administratively disabled without deletion.
goals.outcome: An enabled manager can suspend and restore access without deleting accounts.
goals.success_condition: Real application requests demonstrate filtering, edits, revocation and persistence with no unauthorized mutation.

in_scope: Enabled flag, filter/edit, session revocation and additive SQLite migration
Functional automated tests and local sandbox release
out_of_scope: New role hierarchy or full RBAC

requirements.statement: An enabled account can authenticate and use the account administration view; a disabled account cannot authenticate.
The account view shows and filters enabled status and permits an authenticated enabled manager to change it.
Disabling an account revokes previously issued login sessions on the next protected request; re-enabling it does not resurrect revoked sessions.
The enabled state survives restart; additive migration preserves existing account rows and is idempotent.
Protect authentication and writes with CSRF, reject anonymous and forged sessions and off-site next redirects; retain the teaching example authorization model without a new RBAC system.

acceptance_criteria.condition: Login with enabled versus disabled account credentials
acceptance_criteria.expected_result: Enabled account reaches protected list; disabled login is rejected.

acceptance_criteria.condition: An enabled manager edits another account and filters the list by status
acceptance_criteria.expected_result: Stored status changes and filtered results match database state.

acceptance_criteria.condition: Retain a cookie, disable and re-enable its account
acceptance_criteria.expected_result: Old cookie is rejected both times; fresh login after enable succeeds; unaffected manager retains access.

acceptance_criteria.condition: Restart after a state change and migrate a legacy SQLite table twice
acceptance_criteria.expected_result: State and original rows/IDs remain; migration is idempotent.

acceptance_criteria.condition: Try missing/invalid CSRF, forged/anonymous sessions, off-site next and malformed registration
acceptance_criteria.expected_result: Unauthorized mutation/login fails; logout is POST-only; redirect stays local; no silent account creation.
